dishes.name: Jollof Rice
dishes.description: A one-pot rice dish cooked in a rich tomato and pepper base, seasoned with onions and spices. Arguably Nigeria's most famous export, sold everywhere from roadside buka stalls to owambe parties.

dishes.name: Suya
dishes.description: Skewered, thinly sliced grilled meat coated in a dry pepper-and-groundnut spice blend called yaji. Sold by roadside vendors after dark, often with raw onions and cabbage.

dishes.name: Akara
dishes.description: Deep-fried bean cakes made from blended black-eyed peas, onions, and pepper. A classic Lagos breakfast, usually eaten with pap (akamu) or bread.

dishes.name: Puff-Puff
dishes.description: Sweet, deep-fried dough balls with a crisp outside and fluffy center. A go-to snack sold from trays balanced on vendors' heads across the city.

dishes.name: Boli
dishes.description: Ripe plantain roasted over an open flame, usually served with roasted groundnuts or a spicy pepper sauce called ata rodo.

dishes.name: Moin Moin
dishes.description: A steamed bean pudding made from blended black-eyed peas, peppers, and onions, often studded with boiled egg or fish. Wrapped and steamed in leaves or foil.

dishes.name: Asun
dishes.description: Spicy grilled goat meat, chopped and tossed in a fiery pepper sauce with onions and bell peppers. A popular small-chops and drinking-spot favorite.

dishes.name: Pepper Soup
dishes.description: A light, intensely spiced broth made with catfish, goat meat, or assorted meat and a blend of aromatic pepper soup spices. Popular as a late-night warm-up dish.

dishes.name: Ewa Agoyin
dishes.description: Mashed brown beans served with a smoky, blended pepper sauce fried in palm oil. Traditionally eaten with agege bread or boiled plantain.

dishes.name: Shawarma
dishes.description: Grilled shaved chicken or beef wrapped in flatbread with vegetables, sauce, and sometimes chips. A Lagos late-night street food staple with a local twist.

dishes.name: Chin Chin
dishes.description: Small, crunchy fried dough cubes, lightly sweetened and often flavored with nutmeg. A popular snack for parties and long journeys alike.

dishes.name: Kilishi
dishes.description: Thin sheets of dried, spiced beef coated in a peppery groundnut paste before being sun-dried. A portable, intensely flavored snack sold in markets citywide.

dishes.name: Isi Ewu
dishes.description: A whole goat head delicacy cooked in a thick, spicy palm oil sauce with utazi leaves. A celebratory dish typically shared among friends at local spots.

dishes.name: Meat Pie
dishes.description: A flaky pastry filled with seasoned minced meat, potatoes, and carrots. A grab-and-go favorite sold at bakeries and roadside stands across Lagos.

dishes.name: Zobo
dishes.description: A deep red hibiscus drink infused with ginger, pineapple, and spices, served chilled. The go-to street beverage to cool down from spicier dishes.

dishes.name: Gizdodo
dishes.description: Diced gizzard and fried ripe plantain tossed together in a spicy pepper sauce. A popular small-chops dish at parties and lounges.

dishes.name: Small Chops
dishes.description: An assorted platter of bite-sized fried snacks — spring rolls, puff-puff, samosas, and chicken skewers — a staple at Lagos parties and gatherings.
